name: Frankl union-closed sets conjecture
question: Must a finite nontrivial union-closed family have some element in at least half of its sets?
first_attack: Reproduce exact small-family enumeration; seek an isomorph-free minimal-counterexample lemma or certified entropy inequality
method_title: Replay the object, or mine the census
dispatch_next: The certified mine frankl_orbits quotients the n <= 4 census by ground-set permutations: 4,958 families become 366 orbits at n = 4, and the minimum abundance is exactly 1/2. The next lemma has to generate canonical representatives without enumerating 2^(2^5).
dispatch_why: The frankl_orbits mine has quotiented the n <= 4 census. Naive 2^(2^n) enumeration is still the blocker at n = 5, so the next step is a generator that does not list every family.

campaign.method: Finite family enumeration and entropy inequalities
campaign.hypothesis: Every nontrivial finite union-closed family contains an element in at least half its members.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Verify the exact conjecture for bounded universes before deriving any universal structural reduction.
campaign.next_experiment: The certified mine frankl_orbits quotients the n <= 4 census by ground-set permutations: 4,958 families become 366 orbits at n = 4, and the minimum abundance is exactly 1/2. The next lemma has to generate canonical representatives without enumerating 2^(2^5).
campaign.falsification: An exact union-closed family whose maximum element frequency is less than half the family size.
campaign.blocker: Naive exhaustive enumeration scales as 2^(2^n); structural quotient required.

milestones.title: Frankl threshold verified for ground sets of size <=4
milestones.scope: Finite exhaustive test only; not a proof for arbitrary finite ground sets
milestones.description: Enumerates all 2^(2^4)=65,536 families, filters union closure, checks exact frequencies.

milestones.title: Union-closed families on at most 4 elements, up to relabelling
milestones.scope: Exhaustive range already checked without symmetry; the orbit count is not a general proof
milestones.description: 4,958 nontrivial union-closed families on 4 elements form 366 orbits. Minimum abundance 1/2. A second canonisation, by sorted subset tuples, reproduces the orbit counts.

formal_statement.encodes: Families as bitmasks over ground set {0,…,k−1}; union-closed with a nonempty member implies some x with 2·deg(x) ≥ |F|.

kernel_checked.claim: Exhaustive over all 2, 16 and 256 families on ground sets of size 1, 2, 3 (ground_1, ground_2, ground_3).

discovery_trail.question: How do symmetry reductions change what we can actually verify about union-closed families?

nodes.title: A raw census hides relabeling symmetry
nodes.detail: At n = 4 the unfiltered finite mine records 4,958 families; this counts families that may leave ground elements unused. A full-support count is a different quantity.

nodes.title: Compare canonical encodings under permutations
nodes.detail: Canonical encoding identifies ground-set relabeling orbits. A separate closure-pruned descending construction enumerates full-support families without trying every bitmask.

nodes.title: Reproduce the n = 5 full-support orbit count
nodes.detail: The recorded full-support count is 2,747,402 labeled families and 28,960 relabeling orbits; the latter is separately checked using Burnside's lemma. This is known finite mathematics, not a proof of Frankl.

nodes.title: Test canonical augmentation and independent review
nodes.detail: Obtain independent review of both lemmas and their quantified domain; try pruning noncanonical partial states and independently replaying the resulting orbit count. The conjecture remains open.
